description: Expected bytes derived by hand from the rule text at rc.5 (RC5-A); the reference engine does not yet produce them, so this vector is listed in tests/conformance/pending.json until RC5-B. AGSC-04-19 fixes the emitted YAML profile of `lint --fix` and therefore the bytes of every adoption, every `export --markdown` and every fixed file, and it was cited by NO vector before rc.5 — the most dangerous of the six gaps V9A-26 lists, because adopt-0001 exercises only the five keys adoption writes. `lint --fix` itself is defined in the CLI contract only since rc.5 (AGSC-09-09, V9D-01). Derivation, clause by clause. Line endings: CRLF becomes LF. Trailing newline: the file gains exactly one. Key order is SCHEMA ORDER: first the top-level `properties` order of schema/item.schema.json — type, title, description, status, release, tags, aliases, clusters, lang, date, modified, sources, prov, generated, verified, stale_after, ... — of which this file carries type, title, description, status, tags, prov, stale_after, in that order; then the matching `oneOf` branch's `properties` order (concept: type, description, kind, ...), contributing `kind`, which is why `kind` follows `stale_after` although the author wrote it first; then unknown keys in code-point order, contributing `x-acme-note`, which AGSC-02-05a preserves verbatim. Inside the nested `prov` mapping the order is that $def's `properties` order — origin, agent, model, operator, agreement — so the authored operator/origin pair is emitted origin-first. Block style only, two-space indentation, sequence items indented two spaces under their key (`  - agents`), one space after every `:`, no document markers, no trailing spaces. Scalar style: plain unless the value would re-parse as another type or begins with an indicator character — `stable` is emitted plain although it was authored double-quoted, `human:andrei` is plain because a `:` ends a key only when a space follows it, and the instant stays double-quoted because AGSC-02-04 requires dates and instants to be quoted strings. AGSC-04-20 holds throughout: the authored `tags` array keeps its order, the body prose is untouched, and no key is added, removed or inferred. Applying the fix to its own output changes nothing (AGSC-04-19 idempotence), which the `twice` expectation asserts byte for byte.
